subject: Latency regression — request for service reimbursement and trial extension
messages:
From: Lucy Park <lucy@streamline.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ops@streamline.io
Date: 2026-05-09T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent API latency May 7-8 — impact and request

Hi Jonas,

Wanted to escalate an issue we saw over the weekend. Between 2026-05-07 22:30 UTC and 2026-05-08 03:10 UTC our services observed consistently elevated p95/p99 latency for the Redwood text-generation endpoint serving us in us-west-2. We saw token-level queuing spikes and a number of timed-out requests at peak -- attached are screenshots from our synthetic tests and our internal incident timeline.

Impact summary:
- ~4.2M tokens generated during window; ~11% of requests exceeded our internal 350ms p95 SLA threshold.
- Several customer-forward incidents resulted in churn risk for two mid-market customers.

We need two things from Redwood:
1) Confirmation of SLO deviation and a summary of what happened (logs or an incident write-up).
2) A reasonable commercial remediation — Streamline is asking for either a promotional extension (months of free service equivalent) or platform reimbursement (service credit) to offset customer impact while we work through mitigation.

Attached: latency-screenshots.png, incident-timeline.csv

Thanks — can you confirm next steps and expected timeline for a decision?

—Lucy Park
Head of Platform Reliability, Streamline Inc.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Lucy — thanks for the write-up and attachments, and very sorry you hit this window. We're prioritizing a full review.

Immediate plan:
- Marissa (CS) will triage and confirm the SLO window and provide an internal incident summary.
- I will coordinate commercial remediation options and run them by Rishi for approval.

Can you confirm whether Streamline prefers a fixed platform reimbursement (one-time credit) or a promotional extension (e.g., 2–3 months of equivalent service value)? If you have a preferred dollar-equivalent, include it here — that will speed approvals.

I'll get back to you within 48 hours with a proposed remediation.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Streamline incident triage and remediation options

Rishi / Jonas — quick triage notes based on the logs I pulled and the runtime traces from the serving layer:
- Confirmed elevated tail latency attributed to a mis-routed fallback path on a small subset of instances in the us-west shard during the 2026-05-07 22:30 to 2026-05-08 03:10 UTC window.
- Root cause was an interaction between a kernel fallback path and an autoscaler bounce; it caused short-lived KV-cache misses and higher per-token compute time.
- Impact: ~11% p99/p95 spike for affected tokens (matches Streamline's numbers).

Suggested customer remediation options (pick one for approval):
A) Service reimbursement: issue $7,500 platform credit applied to next invoice + formal incident summary (pdf) delivered to the customer.
B) Promotional extension: grant a two-month trial extension (equivalent to $7,500 in ARR credit) plus 30 days of prioritized support during ramp.
C) Larger goodwill offer (senior approval required): three months of token credits equivalent to $10,000.

I'm recommending option A or B (same cost to us), lean toward A because Streamline noted specific customer churn risk — a clear credit on the next invoice reduces churn friction.

Attachments: incident-summary-20260509.pdf (internal incident write-up we can share).

—Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
